title: how to tell time with analog and digital clocks, using 12- and 24-hour clocks

lesson.title: Telling Time: Clocks, a.m. and p.m., and the 24-Hour Clock

steps.say: Imagine your auntie leaves a note on the fridge: swimming at Kitsilano pool at seven thirty. You look at the clock and it says seven thirty. But wait — is that in the morning before school, or in the evening after dinner? This is exactly why we have a.m. and p.m. The letters a.m. mean the hours from midnight to noon, the morning half of the day. The letters p.m. mean the hours from noon to midnight, the afternoon and evening half. Same clock face, two different halves of the day.

visual.caption: Seven thirty — but is it 7:30 a.m. or 7:30 p.m.?

steps.say: Now let's look closely at the clock face. It is a circle, and the whole trip around that circle is one hour. One hour has sixty minutes. See the twelve big numbers? From one number to the very next number is five minutes. So going all the way around is twelve jumps of five, and twelve times five is sixty. The short fat hand tells you the hour. The long skinny hand tells you the minutes.

visual.caption: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12 — three o'clock, or 3:00

steps.say: Let's read a real time by counting in fives. The short hand is just past the four, so the hour is four. The long hand is pointing at the five. Now count around by fives: five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five. That is five jumps of five minutes, which is twenty-five minutes. So this clock says four twenty-five. We write it as four, two dots, two five.

Sometimes the long hand stops between the numbers, on the tiny little tick marks. Each tiny tick is just one minute. Here the long hand is past the five, which we know is twenty-five minutes, and then two more tiny ticks. Twenty-five plus two is twenty-seven. So this clock says four twenty-seven. Land on the closest number first, then count the little ticks one at a time.

visual.caption: 4:27 — jump to 25, then two tiny ticks more

steps.say: Here is where fractions sneak into time. Because the clock is a circle, we can cut it just like a pizza. Half of the circle is half of sixty minutes, and half of sixty is thirty. So when the long hand has gone halfway around, thirty minutes have passed. If the hour is six, we say half past six, and we write it as six thirty.

visual.caption: Half the circle = half of 60 minutes = 30 minutes (half past)

steps.say: Now cut the pizza into four pieces instead. One quarter of sixty is fifteen, because sixty divided by four is fifteen. Fifteen minutes after the hour is quarter past. And when there are only fifteen minutes left to go, we say quarter to the next hour. Look at this clock: the hour is eight and the minutes are forty-five. Sixty take away forty-five is fifteen, so there are fifteen minutes left until nine. We can call it eight forty-five, or quarter to nine. Both are right!

visual.caption: 8:45 — quarter past would be 15 min, this is quarter to nine

steps.say: On a bus screen or a ferry schedule you might see a time like seventeen thirty. That is the twenty-four hour clock, and it never needs a.m. or p.m., because every hour of the day gets its own number from zero to twenty-three. Morning times look the same: nine fifteen in the morning is written oh nine fifteen. For afternoon and evening, just add twelve. Your soccer game at five thirty p.m. becomes five plus twelve, which is seventeen, so seventeen thirty. To go backwards, subtract twelve: twenty hundred minus twelve is eight, so twenty hundred is eight p.m.

visual.caption: 5:30 p.m. on the clock face = 17:30 on a 24-hour screen

steps.say: One last beautiful idea. Long before clocks, First Peoples here in British Columbia told time by watching the sky. The sun's position told them the time of day, and the moon's cycle, about twenty-nine or thirty days, marked the months. The seasons went around and around, telling people when the salmon would run, when the berries were ripe, when to harvest cedar. Just like our clock face, the year is a circle that keeps turning — and each season is one quarter of that big circle.

visual.caption: One season = a quarter of the year's circle, just like 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour

lesson.answer: The clock is a circle of 60 minutes: count by fives, use a.m. before noon and p.m. after, and add 12 to afternoon hours to get 24-hour time.

practice.question: The SkyTrain sign at your station says the next train to Waterfront leaves at 14:45. Write that time on a regular 12-hour clock with a.m. or p.m., and tell how many minutes you would wait if you arrived at 14:30.
practice.answer: 14:45 is 2:45 p.m., because 14 minus 12 is 2. From 14:30 to 14:45 you wait 15 minutes — a quarter of an hour. (2:45 p.m. is also called quarter to three.)
